receptiveListening: Selected music for relaxation and emotional regulation. Active listening with body movements. Association of music with images and stories.
Repertoire selection for different emotional states. Directed listening for cognitive stimulation. Auditory memory work.

Repertoire adapted for different therapeutic objectives. Listening with expressive movement proposal. Sensory stimulation through music.

musicalImprovisation.label: Musical improvisation
musicalImprovisation.placeholder: Free or guided interaction with instruments...
prompts: Free exploration of instruments followed by gradual structuring. Musical dialogues between therapist and patient. Creation of rhythmic 'conversations'.
Spontaneous interaction with melodic instruments. Development of improvised musical themes. Musical question and answer games.
Free creation with percussion instruments. Emotional expression through improvisation. Exploration of sound textures.
Free vocal improvisation followed by rhythmic structuring. Non-verbal sound dialogues. Creative expression without judgment.

musicalRecreation.label: Musical recreation
prompts: Familiar songs adapted to therapeutic needs. Modification of lyrics to work on specific objectives. Instrumental accompaniment of familiar repertoire.
Reproduction of children's songs with body gestures. Adaptation of tempo and rhythm according to patient's capacity. Inclusion of simple instruments.
Interpretation of patient's favorite songs. Memory work through familiar repertoire. Encouragement of vocal participation.
Recreation of familiar soundtracks. Association of music with daily activities. Development of personalized therapeutic repertoire.

composition.label: Composition
composition.placeholder: Creating music, lyrics or sounds together...
prompts: Creation of small melodies about topics of interest to the patient. Composition of lyrics expressing feelings. Collective construction of simple songs.
Development of personalized sounds and rhythms. Creation of musical stories. Collaborative composition between therapist and patient.
Invention of thematic songs for daily routines. Creation of musical jingles. Development of personal sound identity.
Composition of music to express specific emotions. Creation of soundtracks for favorite activities. Development of original repertoire.

receptiveListening.label: Receptive listening
receptiveListening.placeholder: Listening to music to stimulate emotional or cognitive response...
prompts: Selected music for relaxation and emotional regulation. Active listening with body movements. Association of music with images and stories.

Music for inducing calm states. Listening with directed visualization. Work on identifying emotions through music.
Repertoire adapted for different therapeutic objectives. Listening with expressive movement proposal. Sensory stimulation through music.

movementDance.label: Movement and dance
prompts: Free movements following musical rhythms. Improvised dance for emotional expression. Coordination of movements with different tempos.
Psychomotor activities with music. Exploration of different forms of movement. Body awareness through rhythm.
Structured dances adapted to patient's abilities. Expression of emotions through the body. Sensory-motor integration with musical stimuli.
Movement games with music. Gross motor coordination work. Regulation through rhythmic body activities.

musicalGames.label: Musical games
prompts: Sound imitation games. Musical play to stimulate social interaction. Playful activities with instruments.
Group rhythmic games. Adapted circle games. Cooperative musical activities.
Sound treasure hunt. Musical memory games. Guessing sounds and instruments.
Pulse and coordination games. Musical play for cognitive development. Competitive playful activities with music.
